title: A high-resolution survey of protoplanetary disks in Lupus and the nature of compact disks
question: How small are the dust disks of Class II Lupus protoplanetary disks, how common are substructures in compact disks, and what do sizes, fluxes, dust masses and implied planet masses say about drift-dominated evolution and super-Earth formation

data.angular_resolution: ~0.03 arcsec (~4 au) limits detection of structures

recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration, then separate line and continuum SPWs and average continuum channels
tclean with MTMFS deconvolver and multiscale, weighting chosen per source
key_parameters: Weighting selected per source for highest resolution with sufficient sensitivity

recipe.goal: Measure total continuum flux in the image plane
recipe.method: Aperture photometry with aperture extended until the flux flattens, inclination corrections applied; uncertainty from standard deviation inside each aperture

recipe.goal: Fit visibilities with axisymmetric brightness models
recipe.method: GALARIO visibility modelling with Gaussian, asymmetric-ring, Gaussian+ring or binary (summed two-Gaussian) brightness profiles, plus a delta-like Gaussian for V856ScoA, choosing the simplest structure seen in the image
key_parameters: 48 to 120 walkers, 2,000 to 30,000 steps; first 1,000 steps discarded as burn-in; binaries needed more walkers and iterations
Initial parameters from UVMODELFIT for single disks
Final values are posterior medians with 16th and 84th percentile uncertainties
Inclination and PA fixed to face-on / P.A. fixed to 0 for unresolved or poorly constrained disks
assumptions: Axisymmetric brightness profile; features not visible in the continuum images were not fitted

recipe.goal: Derive total flux, dust radii and the substructure census
recipe.method: Total flux and R68/R90 measured from the modelled images; census of cavities, gaps and rings combining image and visibility analysis
assumptions: Compact disks defined as dust radius < 30 au

recipe.method: Bayesian linear regression of log10 R68 against log10 F_mm with fluxes scaled to 160 pc
assumptions: Flux scaled to a common distance of 160 pc

recipe.goal: Build radiative transfer grid of model disks
recipe.method: RADMC-3D ray-traced images at 1.3 mm for 1728 models; total flux and R68 measured as for observations; optically thin mass compared with input mass; power-law fits outside the saturated region defined by mean optical depth
key_parameters: Grid: 12 dust masses 4e-6 to 5.1e-3 Msun, 12 radii 0.5 to 30 au, 12 stellar luminosities 0.0025 to 3 Lsun, log-uniform
Dust opacities from optool with DSHARP opacities, grain sizes 0.050 um to 3 mm, full scattering matrix
assumptions: Dust surface density proportional to 1/r out to outer radius r_out, Gaussian vertical profile
Stellar effective temperature omitted because it has minimal impact on flux-derived dust mass
Optically thin mass uses kappa = 2.3 cm2/g and uniform T_dust = 20 K

recipe.goal: Infer dust mass and optical depth for compact disks
recipe.method: Invert the model grid on the flux-radius plane using each disk's stellar luminosity, propagating observational uncertainties
key_parameters: 28 disks with radii < 30 au fit within the grid and have known luminosity
assumptions: Stellar luminosities from the stellar-parameters table; disks at the grid edge (binaries, tau >> 5) excluded as indeterminate

recipe.goal: Estimate planet masses for disk substructures
recipe.method: DBNets convolutional neural network applied to continuum FITS images with gap centre positions, inclination, PA and distance
assumptions: Observed gaps and cavities are carved by planets
